Judgment calls: (a) The vertical carrying MOSFET-P 2's gate crosses the y~248 horizontal at x~154-166 with an unmistakable hand-drawn Z-jog (vertical stops at y=250, restarts at y=256, offset laterally) -> CROSSING, not a junction. There is a stray round pen blob sitting ON the horizontal at (155,248) but the jogged wire below starts 6 px lower, so the blob is pen dwell, not a dot. Reading it as a junction would put V-AC 6 and V-AC 7 in parallel across n2/n9 (two voltage sources in one loop, singular matrix), which confirms the hop reading. (b) The crossing at (161,196) (same gate column over the y~195 rail) is a clean 2-px-wide X with no thickening at all -> crossing, so n3 does not touch n4. (c) The crossing at (229,195) IS a junction: the horizontal steps from row 196 to row 195 there and leaves an isolated 5-px-wide ink run at x 228..232 on row 196, i.e. ~3 px of ink beyond the 2-px vertical -- a (partly merged) junction dot, and nothing like the bare 2-px cross at (161,196). So MOSFET-P 2's source column joins the y~195 rail and MOSFET-N 4's drain. (d) Every MOSFET here is drawn with three stubs off the channel bar; the middle stub carries the body arrow and always merges with the far lead on ONE side, and there is a clean 6-10 px white gap in the vertical between the two sides (verified per device at 16-26x for ids 2,3,4,5,9,10), so no device is drain-source shorted. Drain = the stub whose lead runs toward the supply, source = the stub the body arrow shares; this agrees with the arrow convention for all six. (e) MOSFET-P 2's body arrow points AWAY from the channel bar (apex at x~234, barbs at x~228) while MOSFET-N 3's points INTO it (apex at x~115) -- confirms the published P/N classes; no re-classing was needed. (f) MOSFET-N 9 and MOSFET-N 10 are drawn mirrored (channel bar left, gate bar right); their gate leads leave the BOTTOM end of the gate bar, which is the only wire terminus at those points. (g) Terminal order for the 2-terminal parts is as drawn (V-DC 1 left='+' then right; Zener 8 top/cathode then bottom/anode; both V-AC and both I-AC top then bottom); this does not affect any metric. TIER-2 SIM FINDINGS, kept deliberately: nets n7 and n8 each touch only a MOSFET gate and an AC current source, so they have no DC path to ground. The ink is unambiguous -- I-AC 12 wires straight to MOSFET 9's gate bar along y~240, and I-AC 11 wires to MOSFET 10's gate through the small rectangle at (363..405, 313..356) -- and current-source-driven gates are exactly what this AC-analysis drawing shows, so they are left as drawn.
